extracted.intended_audience: U.S. patent examiners and patent applicants/attorneys (patent prosecution practitioners)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for patent examiners (and applicants/attorneys) on recording interview substance, conducting interviews, and handling amendments (signatures, responsiveness, entry, and related procedural requirements) during patent examination and reexamination.

rubrics_metrics.name: PTOL-413 Interview Summary form contents and handling
rubrics_metrics.description: The Interview Summary form PTOL 413 shall be given an appropriate paper number, placed in the right hand portion of the file, and listed on the 'Contents' list on the file wrapper. In a personal interview, the duplicate copy is given to the applicant (or attorney or agent) at the conclusion of the interview; for telephonic, electronic mail, or video conference interviews the copy is mailed to the applicant's correspondence address either with or prior to the next official communication and may be faxed at conclusion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PTOL-413 provides for recordation of: (A) application number; (B) name of applicant; (C) name of examiner; (D) date of interview; (E) type of interview (personal, telephonic, electronic mail, or video conference); (F) name of participant(s); (G) indication whether an exhibit was shown or demonstration conducted; (H) identification of the claims discussed; (I) identification of the specific prior art discussed; (J) indication whether an agreement was reached and description of its general nature (attachments allowed); (K) signature of the examiner who conducted the interview; (K) names of other PTO personnel present. If a complete record of the interview is incorporated in an examiner's amendment, completing PTOL-413 may not be necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reminder of applicant responsibility to record interview substance
rubrics_metrics.description: The PTOL-413 contains a statement reminding the applicant of his or her responsibility to record the substance of the interview.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner should orally remind the applicant of this obligation in each case unless examiner and applicant agree that the examiner will record the substance. If the examiner agrees to record the substance, or it is adequately recorded on PTOL-413 or an attachment, examiner should check the box informing the applicant that no separate record need be submitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Complete and proper recordation of interview substance (minimum required items)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Interview Summary form alone will not be considered complete and proper recordation unless it includes or is supplemented to include all applicable items concerning the substance of the interview.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The substance record should include at least applicable items: (A) brief description of nature of any exhibit shown or demonstration conducted; (B) identification of the claims discussed; (C) identification of specific prior art discussed; (D) identification of principal proposed substantive amendments discussed unless already on PTOL-413; (E) identification of the general thrust of the principal arguments of applicant and examiner (need not be verbatim or highly detailed—sufficient if the general nature or thrust can be understood in context); (F) general indication of any other pertinent matters discussed; (G) if appropriate, general results or outcome of the interview (unless already described on PTOL-413); (H) for interviews via electronic mail, a paper copy of the e-mail contents MUST be made and placed in the file as required by the Federal Records Act.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner review and action on applicant's interview record
rubrics_metrics.description: Examiners are expected to carefully review the applicant's record of the substance of an interview for completeness and accuracy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If record is inaccurate and it bears directly on patentability, the examiner should point it out in the next Office letter or send a letter setting forth the examiner's version. If record is complete and accurate, the examiner should annotate the paper 'Interview record OK' with date and initials. If record is not complete or accurate, the examiner may give applicant a 1-month period to complete the reply under 37 CFR 1.135(c) where the record is in reply to a nonfinal Office action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who may be granted interviews / authority to participate
rubrics_metrics.description: Interviews are not granted to persons lacking proper authority from the applicant or attorney of record on file, and a mere power to inspect is not sufficient authority to grant an interview involving the merits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interviews may be granted to registered individuals who are local representatives of the attorney even if a power of attorney is not on file. If a registered individual has a copy of the application file, the examiner may accept a statement that the person is authorized under 37 CFR 1.34 or is the attorney of record. Interviews normally should not be granted unless the requesting party has authority to bind the principal. Office employees are forbidden to hold oral or written communication with an unregistered, suspended, or excluded attorney or agent regarding an application unless that attorney/agent is the applicant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing and limitations on interviews
rubrics_metrics.description: Except in unusual situations, no interview is permitted after the brief on appeal is filed or after an application has been passed to issue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An interview may be appropriate before applicant's first reply when examiner suggests allowable subject matter or where it helps applicant judge continuing prosecution. Telephone interviews initiated by the examiner to attorneys/agents of record are emphasized. For interviews where notice of allowance has been mailed requests should be granted only with specific Group Director approval upon a written showing of extraordinary circumstances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interviews when examiner lacks negotiation authority
rubrics_metrics.description: For interviews with an examiner who does not have negotiation authority, arrangements should include an examiner who does have such authority and is familiar with the case.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This ensures authoritative agreement may be reached at the time of interview.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grouped interview practice and prompt supplemental amendment for special status
rubrics_metrics.description: For attorneys remote from Washington, D.C., grouped interviews (personal or video conference) can be effective.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a prearranged interview includes agreement to file a prompt supplemental amendment placing the case close to concluding action, prompt filing gives the application special status and brings it up for immediate special action.

rubrics_metrics.name: No discussion of inter partes questions ex parte
rubrics_metrics.description: The examiner may not discuss inter partes questions ex parte with any of the interested parties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protecting exposure of other cases during interview
rubrics_metrics.description: Prior to an interview in the examiner's room, the examiner should arrange the desk so that all files, drawings, and other papers, except those necessary in the interview, are placed out of view.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP § 101 for confidentiality measures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Demonstrations, exhibits, and models handling and recordation
rubrics_metrics.description: A model or demonstration may be exhibited during the interview; if made part of the application record it must comply with 37 CFR 1.91 and be recorded on the 'Contents' portion of the application file wrapper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a model/exhibit is merely used for demonstration and not made part of the record (does not comply with 37 CFR 1.91), a full description of what was demonstrated/exhibited must be made of record per 37 CFR 1.133(b). Demonstrations too large to bring into the Office may be viewed outside the Office with supervisory approval; it is presumed witnessing the demonstration is essential to clarify issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interviews after final rejection — limits and prerequisites
rubrics_metrics.description: Normally one interview after final rejection is permitted, but the intended purpose and content should be presented briefly, preferably in writing, before the interview.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An interview may be granted if the examiner is convinced disposal or clarification for appeal may be accomplished with only nominal further consideration. Interviews merely restating arguments of record or discussing new limitations requiring more than nominal reconsideration or new search should be denied. A second interview may be held if it will expedite issues for appeal or disposal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interviews preceding amendments after application sent to issue (37 CFR 1.312)
rubrics_metrics.description: After an application is sent to issue it is technically no longer under primary examiner jurisdiction; interviews involving detailed consideration of claims sought to be entered and prior art should not be given.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consideration given informally should not exceed what an amendment formally presented would receive; requests for interviews where a notice of allowance has been mailed should be granted only with Group Director approval and a written showing of extraordinary circumstances.

rubrics_metrics.name: When applicant may amend (general times)
rubrics_metrics.description: The applicant may amend: (A) before or after the first examination and action and also after the second or subsequent examination or reconsideration as specified in 37 CFR 1.112; (B) after final rejection, if the amendment meets criteria of 37 CFR 1.116; and (C) when and as specifically required by the examiner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Special rules apply in reexamination proceedings (see MPEP § 2250, § 2266).

rubrics_metrics.name: Signature requirements for amendments
rubrics_metrics.description: An amendment must be signed by a person having authority to prosecute the application; an unsigned or improperly signed amendment will not be entered. See 37 CFR 1.33 and MPEP § 714.01.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Papers must be signed by: (1) an attorney or agent of record appointed per § 1.34(b); (2) a registered attorney/agent not of record acting in a representative capacity under § 1.34(a); (3) assignee of record of entire interest; (4) assignee of record of undivided part interest (with other assignees/applicants as required); or (5) all applicants when no assignee of entire interest. Unsigned/improperly signed amendments are listed on the file wrapper but not entered; the examiner will notify applicant to furnish a duplicate properly signed or ratify the amendment; applicant should be given 1 month under 37 CFR 1.135(c) where appropriate. Problems may sometimes be resolved by calling the local representative. An amendment signed by a person removed from the register under 37 CFR 10.11 is not entered and is submitted to Office of Enrollment and Discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendment signed by an attorney not of record
rubrics_metrics.description: A registered attorney or agent acting in a representative capacity under 37 CFR 1.34 may sign amendments even though he does not have a power of attorney in the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP § 405 and § 402 for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendment signed by applicant when attorney of record exists
rubrics_metrics.description: If an amendment signed by the applicant is received in an application in which there is a duly appointed attorney, the amendment should be entered and acted upon.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attention should be called to 37 CFR 1.33(a) in patent applications and to 37 CFR 1.33(c) in reexamination proceedings. Prepare two copies of the action: send one to the attorney and the other directly to the applicant; annotate 'Copy to applicant' on originals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Replies/amendments must be fully responsive (37 CFR 1.111)
rubrics_metrics.description: After an adverse Office action, to be entitled to reconsideration or further examination the applicant must reply in writing and must reply to every ground of objection and rejection in the prior Office action, distinctly and specifically pointing out supposed errors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reply must present arguments pointing out specific distinctions believed to render the claims patentable over applied references. A general allegation that claims define a patentable invention without specifics does not comply. In amending, applicant must clearly point out patentable novelty in view of references and show how amendments avoid such references. Support for amendments in the disclosure must be specifically pointed out (see MPEP § 2163.06). Formal matters vs merits line is not sharp; some formal corrections may touch merits and be insisted upon prior to indicating allowable subject matter. Claims may be amended by canceling, presenting new claims, or rewriting per 37 CFR 1.121. Replies must appear bona fide to advance the application to final action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner options for amendments not fully responsive and use of 37 CFR 1.135(c)
rubrics_metrics.description: When a reply is a bona fide attempt to advance the application but inadvertently omits some matter, the examiner may give applicant a new time period for reply under § 1.134/1.135(c) to supply the omission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The examiner may: (A) accept the amendment as adequate to avoid abandonment; (B) notify applicant that the reply must be completed within the remaining period for reply to avoid abandonment; or (C) set a new 1-month period for applicant to complete the reply under 37 CFR 1.135(c). Treatment depends on whether amendment is bona fide, whether there is sufficient time remaining, and the nature of the deficiency. Minor omissions may be treated by issuing a new Office action reiterating the unaddressed rejection/requirement. Serious omissions (e.g., unsigned) require notifying applicant to supply omission within remaining time or set a new time period. 37 CFR 1.135(c) applies only to inadvertent omissions and only before final Office action; it does not apply where omission is deliberate. If examiner concludes applicant is attempting to abuse practice to obtain additional time, examiner need only indicate reply must be completed within the original period. After final action, 1.135(c) does not apply; amendments after final are entered only if they place the application in condition for allowance or better form for appeal (see MPEP §§ 714.12-714.13).

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of replies after final action and examiner's amendment authorization
rubrics_metrics.description: The practice under 37 CFR 1.135(c) does not apply after a final Office action. Amendments after final are approved for entry only if they place the application in condition for allowance or better form for appeal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a reply to a final Office action substantially places the application in condition for allowance, the examiner may request authorization from applicant (or representative) for an examiner's amendment to correct omissions and place the application in condition for allowance; in that case the date of the reply is date of such authorization. Examiner also has authority to enter the reply, withdraw the finality of the last Office action, and issue a new Office action (non-final, final, or Ex parte Quayle action) at examiner's discretion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Immediate inspection checklist for amended applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Amended applications filed near the end of the period for reply should be inspected immediately upon filing to determine completeness and to prevent abandonment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When an amended application is put on the examiner's desk it should be inspected to determine: (D) if changes warrant transfer (MPEP § 903.08(d)); (E) if case is special (MPEP § 708.01); (F) if claims suggested to applicant for interference purposes have been copied; (G) if there is a traverse of a restriction requirement (MPEP § 818.03(a)); (H) if 'easily erasable' paper or other nonpermanent method of preparation has been used (MPEP § 714.07); (I) if references cited by applicant (MPEP § 707.05(b) and § 1302.12); (J) if a terminal disclaimer has been filed (MPEP § 508.01, § 804.02, § 804.03, § 1490); (K) if any matter involving security has been added (MPEP § 115).

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplemental action when amendment crosses with Office action
rubrics_metrics.description: If a supplemental amendment is filed on or before the mailing date of the regular action but reaches the examining group later, a supplemental action is usually necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supplemental action should be promptly prepared; need not reiterate all portions of the previous action still applicable but should specify which portions are to be disregarded and point out that the period for reply runs from the mailing of the supplemental action. The action should be headed 'Responsive to amendment of (date) and supplemental to the action mailed (date).'

rubrics_metrics.name: Permanent ink or equivalent requirement for amendments (37 CFR 1.52(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: 37 CFR 1.52(a) requires 'permanent dark ink or its equivalent' be used on papers that become part of the record; 'easily erasable' paper violates the requirement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If noncompliance is discovered when amendment reaches examining group, applicant is promptly notified that amendment is not entered and required to file a permanent copy within 1 month or to order PTO to make a copy at applicant's expense; physical entry will be made from the permanent copy. If discovered later when application is reached for action, similar steps are taken but action on the application is not held up; requirement for permanent copy is included in Office action. Good photocopies or facsimiles on satisfactory paper are acceptable; signatures must be applied after copies if original signature required per 37 CFR 1.4(e). See MPEP § 608.01 for acceptable copies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Telegraphic amendments handling
rubrics_metrics.description: When a telegraphic amendment (telegram) is received it is placed in the file but not entered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant is notified that the telegram is not accepted as a reply to the previous Office action and is not entered. The time period for reply continues to run and is extendable under 37 CFR 1.136.

rubrics_metrics.name: Status of amendments filed before the first Office action
rubrics_metrics.description: An amendment filed before the first Office action but not filed along with the original application does not enjoy the status of part of the original disclosure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: However, an application will be accorded a filing date based upon submission of a complete specification including claims and required drawings. If an application filed under 37 CFR 1.53(b) is filed without a signed oath/declaration and accompanied by an amendment, that amendment is considered part of the original disclosure; a subsequently filed oath/declaration must refer to both the application and the amendment. Any copy of the application as filed must include the amendment where certified copies for priority purposes are requested. Amendments should accompany the application or be filed after the application has received its application number and filing date (see MPEP § 502).
